$comment: Log codes: one per kind of problem or unasked-for end, shown in log lines, bug reports and error details. A code never changes meaning; retired codes stay listed with "retired": true. sources: who logs it (srv server, lk LiveKit via the server, p2p tunnel sidecar via the server, hook webhooks, bug bug inbox, bot built-in bots, app web/phone/desktop app, desk desktop main process, upd desktop updater). docs/log-codes.md is generated from this file (server test LogCodeTests).

codes.meaning: The daily backup failed.
codes.action: Check free disk space and that the world folder's backups/ is writable; Settings → Backups shows the last result.

codes.meaning: A backup couldn't be sent to a backup buddy (why= says what went wrong).
codes.action: Usually the friend's server is offline; it retries on its own. Settings → Backups → Backup buddies shows the details.

codes.meaning: The daily backup couldn't be copied to the extra folder (Backups.CopyTo).
codes.action: Check that the folder or drive is there and writable.

codes.meaning: A removed backup buddy couldn't be told that it no longer keeps our backups.
codes.action: Nothing: it deletes the copies after its grace period anyway.

codes.meaning: Copies kept for a friend's server couldn't be deleted or swept yet.
codes.action: Check the world folder's permissions; it tries again.

codes.meaning: A channel export failed for an unexpected reason (the admin sees "The export couldn't be made").
codes.action: Check free disk space and the world folder's exports/ folder; try the export again. Report a bug if it keeps failing.

codes.meaning: A built-in bot's scheduled work failed (what= names the bot).
codes.action: Report it with the log line; the bot tries again on its next tick.

codes.meaning: An outgoing webhook delivery failed after its retries (why= is the outcome).
codes.action: Check the receiving service; Server settings → Webhooks shows each delivery.

codes.meaning: An outgoing webhook was turned off after failing again and again.
codes.action: Fix the receiving end, then turn the webhook back on in Server settings → Webhooks.

codes.meaning: Queueing or running an outgoing webhook delivery failed unexpectedly.
codes.action: Report it with the log line.

codes.meaning: LiveKit (voice) stopped; it's started again after a pause (exit= is its exit code).
codes.action: If it keeps happening, check that the voice ports are free (Voice.Port, RtcTcpPort, RtcUdpPort).

codes.meaning: LiveKit reported a warning (msg= is its own wording, scrubbed).
codes.action: Usually harmless; report it if voice misbehaves at the same time.

codes.meaning: A request to LiveKit (remove someone, change permissions, close a room) failed.
codes.action: Usually LiveKit was restarting; check for LK-110 around it.

codes.meaning: livekit-server wasn't found, so voice is off.
codes.action: Put livekit-server next to iskra-server, or set Voice.LiveKitPath or ISKRA_LIVEKIT.

codes.meaning: Starting or running LiveKit failed.
codes.action: Check that livekit-server can run on this machine; report it with the log line.

codes.meaning: LiveKit reported an error (msg= is its own wording, scrubbed).
codes.action: Report it with the log line if voice misbehaves.

codes.meaning: Trimming the log files failed.
codes.action: Check that the world folder's logs/ is writable.

codes.meaning: A captions or translation model from upstream failed its check and wasn't kept.
codes.action: Nothing: it's fetched again on the next request. Report it if it repeats.

codes.meaning: The router didn't open every port (UPnP / NAT-PMP), or couldn't be searched for.
codes.action: Forward the ports by hand (docs/hosting.md) or turn on UPnP in the router.

codes.meaning: The public address is shared with other customers (carrier-grade NAT): ports can't be opened.
codes.action: Use "Let friends connect without port forwarding" (p2p), or ask the provider for a public IPv4 address.

codes.meaning: The router stopped answering; it's searched for again.
codes.action: Nothing, unless it repeats: then restart the router.

codes.meaning: The internet hosting check failed unexpectedly.
codes.action: Report it with the log line; it tries again soon.

codes.meaning: Removing a port from the router failed.
codes.action: Nothing: the router drops it when its lease ends.

codes.meaning: A push notification couldn't be delivered (status= from the push service).
codes.action: Usually the push service was unreachable; repeated 4xx means the subscription is stale.

codes.meaning: A scheduled job failed (what= names it: polls, events, reminders, AFK, rooms, teams...).
codes.action: Report it with the log line; the job runs again on its next tick.

codes.meaning: A connection was refused at the handshake (why= is the protocol error code).
codes.action: Nothing on its own; many in a row from one app mean it has an old invite or a revoked device.

codes.meaning: A session ended without the app asking (why=: kicked, removed, socket-lost, stalled, bad-frames, too-large, aborted).
codes.action: Nothing on its own; socket-lost in a row for one acct points at that person's network.

codes.meaning: A client stopped reading and was dropped (its queue was full).
codes.action: Nothing: the app reconnects and catches up.

codes.meaning: A session crashed.
codes.action: Report it with the log line (name= and frame= say where).

codes.meaning: A warning or error from a component that has no code of its own (often ASP.NET itself).
codes.action: Report it with the log line.

codes.meaning: A request handler failed (op= is the request type); the app got "Something went wrong on the server".
codes.action: Report it with the log line (name= and frame= say where).

codes.meaning: The server couldn't open its world folder and didn't start (why=: settings-json, database, no-access, files).
codes.action: The console says what to do; for a damaged database, restore a backup.

codes.meaning: A Discord import failed unexpectedly.
codes.action: Report it with the log line.

codes.meaning: A cleanup sweep failed (retention, uploads, disappearing messages).
codes.action: Report it with the log line; it runs again later.

codes.meaning: A file due for deletion couldn't be deleted yet (in use, or no access).
codes.action: Nothing: it's tried again on the next sweep.

codes.meaning: Getting a Let's Encrypt certificate failed.
codes.action: Check that port 80 reaches this server from the internet and that the domain points here.

codes.meaning: Https.BindAddress / ProxyProtocol settings are ignored because HTTPS is off.
codes.action: Set Https.Mode to "acme" or "files", or remove those settings.

codes.meaning: Bound to localhost without the PROXY protocol: every client looks like this machine.
codes.action: Behind a proxy, turn on Https.ProxyProtocol (docs/hosting.md).

codes.meaning: The stored certificate couldn't be read and is ignored.
codes.action: Delete the certs/ folder's files to get a new one, or fix their permissions.

codes.meaning: A connection on a PROXY protocol listener was dropped (at most once a minute).
codes.action: Check the proxy's proxy_protocol setting and Https.ProxyTrustedFrom.

codes.meaning: The peer-to-peer tunnel stopped; it's started again after a pause (exit= is its exit code).
codes.action: If it keeps happening, report it with the p2p lines around it.

codes.meaning: iskra-p2p wasn't found, so friends can't connect without port forwarding.
codes.action: Put iskra-p2p next to iskra-server, or set P2p.SidecarPath.

codes.meaning: The peer-to-peer tunnel failed (to start, or it reported failed; nat= the NAT type it last saw: open, consistent, randomized).
codes.action: Report it with the p2p lines around it.

codes.meaning: Checking GitHub for server updates failed.
codes.action: Nothing: it checks again in an hour.

codes.meaning: Installing a server update failed; the server keeps running its current version.
codes.action: Try again from Settings → Updates; report it if it repeats.

codes.meaning: A server update didn't start and was undone (rolled back).
codes.action: Report it with the version (to=).

codes.meaning: Someone was removed from a voice room they may not be in (permissions, timeout, rules, limit).
codes.action: Nothing: this is the server enforcing the channel's rules.

codes.meaning: The connection to a server closed or failed; the app retries.
codes.action: Look at close= and why= and the server's SES lines for the same conn=.

codes.meaning: The handshake with a server timed out: the socket opened but no welcome came within 30 s (path= says direct or tunnel).
codes.action: Check the server is up; through a tunnel, look at the TUN lines around it.

codes.meaning: The server is restarting.
codes.action: Nothing: the app reconnects.

codes.meaning: The server stopped (close 1001).
codes.action: Nothing: the app reconnects when it's back.

codes.meaning: The server refused the connection (code= is the protocol error code).
codes.action: Depends on the code: an expired invite, a ban, a revoked device.

codes.meaning: The app stopped trying (gave up, or the server was removed).
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: Opening a peer-to-peer tunnel to a server failed.
codes.action: Check the host's p2p status; very strict networks block it.

codes.meaning: The direct address didn't answer (why=: timeout, refused, http-<status>, not-iskra; took=); using the tunnel.
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: A connection through the peer-to-peer tunnel couldn't be made (why= is the DHT's reason: peer-not-found, holepunch-aborted, holepunch-double-randomized-nats...; nat= ours). At most once a minute per reason.
codes.action: peer-not-found: the host is offline or its tunnel isn't announced. Holepunch reasons: both networks are strict (randomized NAT); try another network on one side.

codes.meaning: The tunnel's voice link (TURN carried over the tunnel) closed; it's made again with the next voice packet (dur= how long it lasted).
codes.action: Nothing unless it repeats; then look for TUN-160 and VOI-140 around it.

codes.meaning: Joining voice failed (token, connect, timeout).
codes.action: Check the server's LK lines around the same time.

codes.meaning: Voice's network route (ICE), on connect and whenever it changes: ice= our candidate type (host, srflx, prflx, relay), peer= the server's, proto= udp or tcp, via=turn when it goes through a TURN relay (turn= its protocol). As a WARN (why=no-route): no route was found.
codes.action: Nothing for host/srflx over udp. via=turn or proto=tcp works but adds delay; no-route: check the voice ports (UDP and TCP) or the TURN relay.

codes.meaning: Voice is losing packets: incoming loss stayed over 5% for 20 s (loss= percent, the worst sample; at most once in 5 minutes).
codes.action: Usually the network (Wi-Fi, a busy uplink, a mobile hotspot). Compare with the voice route (VOI-130) and the other people's logs.

codes.meaning: Voice is slow: the round trip to the voice server stayed over 300 ms for 20 s (rtt=; at most once in 5 minutes).
codes.action: Usually distance or a relayed route (via=turn in VOI-130); a wired connection helps.

codes.meaning: A voice channel's recording mark ended without anyone stopping it (why=left: the recorder left; permission: they lost recordVoice or access; max: 4 hours; timeout or declined: an encrypted channel's people didn't all agree; encrypted, channel, unavailable). The recorder's app stops recording too.
codes.action: Nothing: this is the server keeping the mark honest. The audit log has the same end (voice.record.stop).

codes.meaning: The desktop app stopped recording a call by itself (why=disk: under 500 MB free; write: a file couldn't be written; folder: the folder couldn't be made; max: 4 hours).
codes.action: Free up disk space or pick another folder (Record → Folder). What was recorded until then is kept.

codes.meaning: Voice is reconnecting (signal lost).
codes.action: Nothing unless it repeats.

codes.meaning: Left voice: the same account joined from another device.
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: Left voice: removed or moved by a moderator.
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: Left voice: the room closed or the server is restarting.
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: Left voice: the connection was lost.
codes.action: Check the network; see VOI-130.

codes.meaning: Left voice: another account signed in on this device joined voice (one account in voice at a time).
codes.action: Nothing.

codes.meaning: The microphone's noise suppression fell back to RNNoise (why=: start-failed, slow; kind=cpu with count= the realtime load in percent, or kind=late when its frames kept coming back late).
codes.action: Nothing; report it if the microphone sounds wrong.

codes.meaning: An audio or video device was lost or changed during a call.
codes.action: Pick the device again in Settings → Voice.

codes.meaning: Decrypting encrypted voice failed.
codes.action: Rejoin the channel; report it if it repeats.

codes.meaning: The desktop app couldn't check for updates.
codes.action: Nothing: it checks again later.

codes.meaning: Installing a desktop app update failed.
codes.action: Download the app again from iskra.foo.

codes.meaning: A known step failed (area= and op= say which, name= and frame= where; msg= is the browser's own wording).
codes.action: Report it with the bug report.

codes.meaning: Voice activity detection couldn't start; the microphone uses the volume threshold instead.
codes.action: Nothing; report it if voice activity misbehaves.

codes.meaning: Cleaning incoming voices isn't available here (or fell back, why= says why).
codes.action: Nothing; others' voices play as they come.

codes.meaning: Captions, a transcript or a translation couldn't start or stopped (what= says which).
codes.action: Try again; on slow devices turn it off.

codes.meaning: The camera background effect couldn't start or was turned off (why= says why).
codes.action: Nothing; the camera keeps working without it.

codes.meaning: The microphone couldn't be captured or sent; you stay muted.
codes.action: Check the microphone permission and device in Settings → Voice.

codes.meaning: The assistant couldn't get an answer from the AI provider the user chose (why= auth, rate, network, http, timeout, bad_response or blocked; status= the provider's HTTP status).
codes.action: Check the key, address and model in My settings → Assistant; a model on this computer may need to allow requests from Iskra (docs/assistant.md).

codes.meaning: A local MCP client couldn't connect to the desktop app (why= auth, off, busy or socket).
codes.action: Turn on Allow local MCP clients in My settings → Assistant, keep Iskra open, and add the server again with the command shown there.

codes.meaning: A part of the desktop app stopped unexpectedly (kind=: page, gpu, utility; reason= from Electron).
codes.action: If the window went blank, open it again from the tray (or restart the app); report it if it repeats.

codes.meaning: A server hosted in the desktop app stopped without being asked (exit= is its exit code).
codes.action: Look at that server's logs/ folder for the same time.

codes.meaning: A server hosted in the desktop app couldn't start (why=).
codes.action: Look at server.log and logs/ in that server's folder.

codes.meaning: The desktop app couldn't save its settings.
codes.action: Check that the app's data folder is writable.

codes.meaning: The app's window stopped responding for a while.
codes.action: Nothing unless it repeats; then report it with the bug report.

codes.meaning: A bot run by the desktop app (My settings → Bots on this PC) stopped without being asked (exit= is its exit code).
codes.action: Open the bot's log in Bots on this PC: its last lines say why.

codes.meaning: A bot run by the desktop app couldn't start (why=: no-entry, no-python, spawn, not-trusted: the person said no in the confirm dialog).
codes.action: For your own folder: check it has a package.json main, bot.js or bot.py; Python bots need Python 3.11+ installed.

codes.meaning: An uncaught error in the desktop app's main process.
codes.action: Report it with the log lines around it.

codes.meaning: An uncaught error (area unknown).
codes.action: Report it with the bug report.
